Speaking: Yngya (she/her)

Conversation_NPC/Yngya/Woolhaven/1:
Speaking: Yngya (she/her)
 She hid Woolhaven away from the world. The "prophecy" is the prohecy that plays at the start of the base game: "Praise the Lamb, conduit to great power, promised liberator of the One Who Waits below..." that lead to all the lambs being killed by the Bishops.

Speaking: Yngya (she/her)

Lore/Lore_15/Lore: These research tablets are written like Marchosias, who is an alchemist/scientist, is jotting down his notes while researching. He is writing notes about Woolhaven (abandoned graves and ruins) and Ewefall (harsh and snowy). He finds this place suitable to live in because there are no Gods here (this is written prior to Yngya's return). He has been experimenting with lightning (the Charged Shards resource) and tried to use the power of electricity//lightning to "liberate/free" other Followers, but so far has not been successful.
Lore/Lore_15/Name: Name for a piece of lore relating to Marchosias
Lore/Lore_16/Lore: The Executioner is writing about when they beheaded the Lamb (player) at the start of the base game, and how the Lamb didn't die. She hopes that the player doesn't find her.

Lore/Lore_17/Lore: Aniel is writing about Baraq here. NOTE FOR LORE_17-LORE_22; the words in the color tags in these lore notes when put together read "we will not rest we will rot instead this broken world deserves to end." If you could please recreate this word puzzle in your language, that would be amazing!

Lore/Lore_18/Description: Description of a lore note written by Aniel; she wrote these messages in the few days before all the Woolhaven NPCs died.
Lore/Lore_18/Lore: Aniel is writing about herself here, which is why she striked out the first person "I could not" and tries to replace it with the third person "she could not" but she gives up quickly.

Written by Marchosias, he says that he has delivered more Charged Shards to Rami to make into Gauntlets (the Legendary Weapon gauntlets) so he can use the power of the Charged Shards to liberate Followers from Gods; he writes in this note that 2/3 of his experiment subjects have been successfully liberated, and the third has become mute. He is referring to the minibosses Festor, Mestor, and Nestor.

Notifications/UpgradeRitualReady: A notification that you can now perform a ritual to upgrade yourself

Notifications/Winter/Coming/1: Notification that a moderate winter (no blizzards, but will snow under structures) will be arriving tomorrow
Notifications/Winter/Coming/2: Notification that a severe winter (potential blizzards, will snow under structures) will be arriving tomorrow

Tutorial UI/Winter_1:
Tutorial Title: Winter 1.
Note that "winter 1" does not refer to the first Winter the player experiences, but the first level of winter the player experiences (Winter Level 1). Winter increments in difficulty as the player progresses through the game. So the player could do many level 1 winters until they reach the point in the game where winter gets harder.
Tutorial UI/Winter_1/Description: Tutorial Information: In Winter 1, Followers can start freezing if they get cold enough. Freezing is a Follower state that Followers enter when cult warmth drops too low, the same way Illness works in the Cult.
Tutorial UI/Winter_1/Info1: Tutorial Information: If the Rotburn Furnace is empty, Followers will be cold, and then if the Rotburn Furnace is still not filled with Rotburn, Followers will become freezing.
Tutorial UI/Winter_2/Description: Tutorial Information: Winter has gotten stronger
Tutorial UI/Winter_2/Info1: Tutorial Information: Blizzards (snow storms) can now occur in winter; if the player fills their Rotburn Furnace up to full, the blizzard will disappear.
Tutorial UI/Winter_3/Description: Tutorial Information: Winter has gotten stronger
Tutorial UI/Winter_3/Info1: Tutorial Information: wolves can attack the ranch in the player's cult base. They run in from the bushes around the cult and go straight for the ranch animals.
Tutorial UI/Winter_4/Description: Tutorial Information: structures within the Cult can become covered in snow
Tutorial UI/Winter_4/Info1: Tutorial Information: players can build the Heater (translated already in full loc kit in Structures tab, string PROXIMITY_FURNACE) structure to thaw snowed under structures
Tutorial UI/Winter_5/Description: Tutorial Information: "howling" is a way of describing a storm, because the strong wind sounds like howling.

UI/Credits/Acknowledgement:
In Australia, because the country has a strong and old Indigenous population since before colonisation, it's good practice to have an Acknowledgement of Country included in big projects that are made here as a way of showing respect to the Traditional Owners (Indigenous people) of the land, and showing that we acknowledge their long histories and continuing connecting to this place that was almost lost due to European settlement, but still survives.
 
 Acknowledgements of Country differ in wording, but there are good examples here of how other languages can translate this (I can't find a Chinese or French Canadian resource, unfortunately).
 
 It's important to be as respectful as possible, including using proper nouns, when referring to the following: Traditional Custodians, Country, Elders, Aboriginal.
 
 The message is essentially this: "some parts of this game were created across the many different Aboriginal lands of Australia (while Australia is recognised internationally as 1 country/nation, there are hundreds of different Aboriginal groups who live here). We honour and pay our respects to the Traditional Custodians (the native people of the land, who have taken care of this place for a long time) of Country ("Country" here does not just refer to the physical land, but to the physical, cultural, and spiritual components of a homeland). We give our respects to Elders (seniors in Aboriginal and First Nations communities) of the past and present, and to the stories and history that they have kept alive since before anyone can remember. Sovereignty was never ceded (their authority was never given up) and this always has been and always will be Aboriginal land (their place/country/land)."
